Content:
We can compute a data set's lower and upper quartiles and interquartile range using its dot plot.

Content:
Let's compute the lower quartile of the data set with the following dot plot:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8404657ed65fac4511267536e0beaba8]

Content:
Notice that the number of data points ([MATH: 9]) is odd. As a result,

Content:
- the median is the [MATH: 5]th value in the data set, and
- we can separate the data into its lower and upper parts (both excluding the median) as illustrated below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b274652f57029d5c582bfaac7b99a467]

Content:
The lower quartile is the median of the lower part, so let's focus on that part only:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/135a094b3a435d122392f3a099a90ecd]

Content:
We now find the median of the lower part. Since the lower part has an even number of points, the lower quartile is the mean of the two middle numbers (the second and the third numbers in this case):

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0df35f4cd7177168f42cb3f70984791e]

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \text{lower quartile} = \dfrac{{\color{red}3}+{\color{red}4}}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2} = 3.5.]

Find the interquartile range for the distribution represented by the dot plot above.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Method 1

Notice that the number of data points ([MATH: 7]) is odd. As a result, we can separate the data into its lower and upper parts, as illustrated in the diagram below.

  • The lower quartile is the median of the lower part. In this case, it's just the middle number. Therefore, [MATH: \text{lower quartile} = 8,] as shown in the diagram on the left.

  • The upper quartile is the median of the upper part. In this case, it's also the middle number. Therefore, [MATH: \text{upper quartile} = 16,] as shown in the diagram on the right.

So, the interquartile range is [MATH: \text{upper quartile} - \text{lower quartile} = 16 - 8 = 8.]

Method 2

The dot plot represents the following data:

[MATH: 4, \: 8, \: 12, \: 16, \: 16, \: 16, \: 20]

Since the number of data points is odd ([MATH: 7]), the median of the data set is the middle number (the [MATH: \color{blue}4]th value).

Now, we find the quartiles.

  • The lower part consists of every data point below the median: [MATH: \underbrace{4, \: 8, \: 12,}_{\text{lower part}} \: {\color{blue}16}, \: 16, \: 16, \: 20]

  • The lower quartile is the median of the lower half. In this case, it's just the middle number: [MATH: 4, \: {\color{red}\underline{8}}, \: 12] Therefore, [MATH: \text{lower quartile} = 8.]

  • The upper part consists of every data point above the median: [MATH: 8, \: 8, \: 12, \:{\color{blue}16}, \: \underbrace{16, \: 16, \: 20}_{\text{upper part}}] The upper quartile is the median of the upper part. In this case, it's also just the middle number: [MATH: 16, \:{\color{red}\underline{16}}, \: 20] Therefore, [MATH: \text{upper quartile} = 16.]

Finally, the interquartile range is [MATH: \text{upper quartile} - \text{lower quartile} = 16 - 8 = 8.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can compute a data set's lower and upper quartiles and interquartile range using its dot plot.

Content:
Let's compute the lower quartile of the data set with the following dot plot:

Content:
Notice that the number of data points ([MATH: 9]) is odd. As a result,

Content:

- we can separate the data into its lower and upper parts (both excluding the median) as illustrated below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b274652f57029d5c582bfaac7b99a467]

Content:
The lower quartile is the median of the lower part, so let's focus on that part only:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/135a094b3a435d122392f3a099a90ecd]

Content:
We now find the median of the lower part. Since the lower part has an even number of points, the lower quartile is the mean of the two middle numbers (the second and the third numbers in this case):

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/0df35f4cd7177168f42cb3f70984791e]

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \text{lower quartile} = \dfrac{{\color{red}3}+{\color{red}4}}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2} = 3.5.]

Item 2 — Tutorial: Measuring Quartiles Using Dot Plots: Method II

Content:

Content:

Graphic:

The dot plot represents the following data:

Content:

The lower quartile is the median of the lower part. In this case, it's the mean of the two middle numbers:

Content:

Content:
So, the lower quartile is
